newsitem.title: ALGERIA: U.N. observers criticise aspects of Algerian poll.
newsitem.headline: U.N. observers criticise aspects of Algerian poll.

text.p: United Nations observers, in a statement published on Monday, criticised the conduct of parts of Algeria's general election in which pro-government parties swept to a majority in the new parliament.
The statement said some observers had problems moving freely during monitoring the poll, and there were questions over voting by security forces and at mobile polling stations.
The U.N. team cancelled a news conference in Algiers on Sunday when they had been due to give their verdict on the election.
Instead, a statement was issued which one of the observers said on Monday was "not about giving a judgment on the fairness of the elections. This is up to the Algerian people.
"It gives facts and observations about the election."

The statement published by two local newspapers said: "While observers were able to move without fear or threats, several had difficulties to carry out their work with all the independence and free movement necessary to assess objectively these elections."
The statement said the observers also questioned what happened in the special voting buros, where security forces cast their ballots early.
"The majority of observers who supervised them share the opinion that the process did not provide sufficient guarantees for neutrality and transparency," the statement said.

Almost all the opposition parties complained after last Thursday's poll of irregularities in the election, which the authorities hope will end more than five years of violence they blame on Moslem fundamentalists.

The statement said the "observers were impressed by the material and logistical preparation for the election, the professionalism of members of the voting offices and the harmony in which the poll took place."
They also praised the efforts by the government to deploy mobile polling stations to reach nomads and other isolated communities in the vast country, but added:
"However several political parties pointed out to observers the lack of information about the hours and itinaries of the 'caravans' and also the fact they were not allowed to accompany them. "

The statement also spoke of problems in some areas during vote counting. It said: "Most observers were able to follow the whole process without a major problem while others saw themselves refused access by some electoral commissions at the provincial level."
It added: "Because of the short period during which most of the observers were present in Algeria it was impossible for the most part to fully supervise the campaign."
